H1.note: the chain starts at 'RLS-associated MEIS1 variation'; its first step is unsigned by the run's own note, and H1.2 (normal development) does not reach H1.3 (abnormal development)

H2.note: BTBD9 from 'BTBD9 dysfunction' in the mechanism; the title names BTBD9 risk variants but the chain starts at the protein. No claim for ACO1: the title ('acts through ACO1-dependent iron sensing to alter') and the mechanism ('changes ACO1-dependent iron-responsive RNA control') give it no direction; a loss reading exists only in the chain step H2.3 ('pathway dysfunction') and the falsification ('restore ACO1 iron-sensing activity'), and a claim signed from a chain step agrees with its own arm by construction

H3.note: the chain starts at 'RLS-associated PTPRD variation'; its first step is unsigned and the mechanism says the direction on PTPRD is unresolved

findings.detail: H1.2 ends at 'normal neural and sleep–wake circuit development' (a process), H1.3 starts at 'abnormal sleep–motor circuit development' (an abnormal phenotype, and sleep–motor rather than sleep–wake); no route from MEIS1 to RLS even before the unsigned first step.

H2.2 ends at iron-responsive RNA regulation and iron homeostasis, H2.3 starts at 'BTBD9–ACO1 pathway dysfunction'; iron never appears again, so the composed BTBD9 arms (S7→S11, S8→S12) skip ACO1 and iron, the hypothesis's whole point.

Both chains start with an association of unknown polarity between the risk variation and the gene, which the run itself says is unestablished, so neither variant claim can compose a signed arm (no route).

Rated high, but every chain citation is excluded (the GWAS rows say nothing about MEIS1 regulation, UniProt says nothing neural, the RLS-model record has no publication), step 1 is unsigned and steps 2 and 3 do not connect.
Rated high, but only H3.2 (PTPRD induces synaptic differentiation, by similarity) keeps a citation; H3.1, H3.3 and H3.4 have none, and step 1 is unsigned.

The BTBD9–ACO1 link rests on one STRING edge (combined 0.45, unsigned); no cited text puts ACO1 in RLS, neurons, electrophysiology or sleep, and the run's own contradicting record finds no ACO1 variant among RLS associations.
Ten GWAS rows are cited for mechanism steps (variant → gene regulation, phenotype → RLS); each states only that an allele goes with RLS, a link no step of the run makes.

Alliance 'model of RLS' records for Meis1 and Btbd9 genotypes (no publication, as the run notes) are cited for 'abnormal circuit development → RLS' and 'abnormal electrophysiology/sleep → RLS'; they name neither phenotype.

UniProt O00470 says MEIS1 is required for hematopoiesis, megakaryocyte lineage development and vascular patterning, not neural development; the Meis1 mouse records are brain morphology and sleep/wake cycle, not circuit development.

HPA expression levels are cited for 'PTPRD required for synaptic differentiation'; Ptprd knockout phenotypes (enhanced LTP, paired-pulse facilitation, impaired swimming) are cited for 'disrupted synaptic differentiation → abnormal gating' but name neither the subject nor gating.

PMID:17637780 (supporting) reports MEIS1 and BTBD9 intronic variants raising RLS risk by more than 50%, and MEIS1 in limb development; no step claims variant → RLS or limb development, so the run's best evidence sits outside its chains.
PMID:30363981 (supporting) is a review abstract on iron in RLS; it names neither ACO1 nor BTBD9 and states no step.

The mechanism says the direction on PTPRD is unresolved, yet the title ('PTPRD risk disrupts') and steps 2 to 4 compose PTPRD →+ synapse assembly →− abnormal gating →+ RLS, i.e. loss of PTPRD raises risk.
H2.3 gives 'restless legs syndrome susceptibility' as the disease state of a step whose object then leads to RLS in H2.4; dropped, as it would make the chain presuppose its conclusion.
Only genes carry CURIEs; every process and phenotype node is ungrounded, and the disease is written 'EFO:MONDO_0005391', a MONDO id under an EFO prefix.
rs6477358-T, the GWAS Catalog's 'risk allele', has beta 'decrease' (lower RLS in women), yet it is cited as RLS risk variation alongside risk-raising alleles.

Six steps carry tissue 'brain' and H3.2 'excitatory and inhibitory neurons' as context; the brain texts the run cites (HPA: PTPRD enriched in brain excitatory and inhibitory neurons; Meis1 abnormal brain morphology; a Purkinje-cell Pcp2-cre Btbd9 knockout) say where the genes are expressed or were perturbed, but none limits a step's result to brain, and the UniProt and Aco1 texts are not brain-specific; dropped as setting, not limitation.
Two of the six question genes (GLIPR1, GABARAPL2) get no hypothesis, and ACO1 enters only through a STRING edge to BTBD9, not through any RLS evidence of its own.

BLN:MEIS1-RLSRiskAlleles and BLN:PTPRD-RLSRiskAlleles stand for the classes 'RLS-associated MEIS1/PTPRD variation'; the run names no single variant at the chain start, and no ontology has a locus-level risk-allele class.

HP has no abnormal sensorimotor gating, abnormal synaptic plasticity or abnormal nervous system development in the formation sense (HP:0012759 is about milestones), so these human-claim nodes are grounded with MP terms (MP:0002634, MP:0004859, MP:0003861).

Allele-level GWAS rows (rs113851554-T beta up, etc.) cannot be evidence for a class-of-variants node; there is no member-of-class link, so the run's strongest data cannot reach the H1 and H3 claims even as a bridge.
Mediation ('BTBD9 acts through ACO1') has no form; splitting the compound 'BTBD9–ACO1 pathway' per gene lets BTBD9 compose to RLS without ACO1, so the arm does not test the hypothesis's mechanism.
A disjunctive object ('altered PTPRD regulation or function') can only be split into two statements, which asserts both parts (S13, S14).

The contradicting GWAS:ACO1:no-association bears on ACO1 → RLS, which is neither a step nor (lacking a stated direction) a claim; the format has no place for evidence about a gene–disease link outside a step, so it can only be excluded (put on S9).
The guide treats 'no association' as a refuting null, but this record is absence from a 532-row catalogue, not a tested null; there is no rule for absence-of-hit records.

The 'abnormal X' rule covers objects ('leads to abnormal X'); for subjects ('abnormal X development leads to RLS') and for a step 'required for normal X' followed by 'abnormal X → ...' there is no rule linking a process to its abnormal phenotype, so such chains never connect.

MGI 'abnormal X' annotations are listed as no_direction, but when the step's object is itself the abnormal-X phenotype a mutant annotation states it (kept, S7, S8); for 'required for X homeostasis' an 'abnormal X homeostasis' knockout arguably implies loss, yet is excluded (S6).
MGI records give the allele symbol (tm1d, tm1c with Pcp2-cre, Gt, em1) but not whether it is a null or which cells; reading 'loss of BTBD9' from tm1d is nomenclature, not text.
The guide gives STRING edges curatedDb only for binds statements; H2.1 is an unsigned association with experimental channel 0.41, kept as curatedDb for want of a kind.
Alliance 'curated as a model of <disease>' records (no publication, no direction) have no row in the evidence-kind table and no exclusion category of their own.
Bridges may quote GO, HP or MONDO definitions but not MP, though MP terms are used for nodes; MP:0003861's definition ('impaired or altered growth') half-links development to its abnormal phenotype.

Using the variant class as claim subject when the chain starts there gives 'no route' for H1 and H3, though H3's gene-level chain composes (PTPRD → RLS, neg); the guide allows no second, gene-level claim.

H2 is about BTBD9 and ACO1, but its title ('alter') and mechanism ('changes ACO1-dependent iron-responsive RNA control') give ACO1 no direction; only the chain step H2.3 ('pathway dysfunction') and the falsification ('restore ACO1 activity') imply loss, so ACO1 gets no claim.

H2.4 makes abnormal sleep behaviour a cause of RLS, but the run's own supporting PMID:17637780 lists disturbed sleep among the features RLS is 'characterized by'; the step turns a feature into a cause.

Single low-grade records reach the top verdict: one STRING edge (combined 0.45, kept as curatedDb) makes S4 'established' at b 4/5, and one mouse MGI annotation each makes the human-phenotype statements S7 and S8 'established', S8's from a Purkinje-cell-only (Pcp2-cre) knockout.

audit.before: claims: BTBD9 neg and ACO1 neg on RLS risk; note: ACO1's direction read from H2.3 'BTBD9–ACO1 pathway dysfunction' and the falsification's 'restore ACO1 iron-sensing activity'
audit.after: claims: BTBD9 neg only; note says ACO1 gets no claim because title and mechanism give it no direction
audit.reason: The guide takes claim sign from the title or mechanism, and says to give no claim when no direction is stated. The title says 'alter' and the mechanism says 'changes ACO1-dependent iron-responsive RNA control', with no sign for ACO1. Signing the claim from chain step H2.3 makes the ACO1 arms (S9→S11, S10→S12) agree with it by construction, so the sign check tests nothing. H2 arms drop from 4 to 2.

audit.reason: False as written. HPA:ENSG00000153707 (cited at H3.2) reports enrichment in brain excitatory and inhibitory neurons, and AGR:MGI:104717:MP:0002152 is about brain morphology. Dropping the context is still right, but for a different reason.

audit.reason: a hypothesis about two genes that states a direction for only one is a hypothesis-agent result

The run's own supporting abstract PMID:17637780 says RLS is 'characterized by ... disturbed sleep'. That makes sleep disturbance a feature, which H2.4 treats as a cause. It is not attached as evidence because it does not state the step.
